goal: Explain why there is no visual XAML designer for this WinUI 3 desktop project and give practical design-time alternatives.
must_include: Says the missing designer is expected for WinUI 3 XAML and is not caused by the shown project file or XAML markup.
Recommends editing XAML directly and using runtime aids such as XAML Hot Reload, Live Visual Tree, or the WinUI 3 Gallery/examples to iterate on layout.
Keeps the project as a WinUI 3 desktop app unless the developer explicitly chooses a different framework for designer support.
Mentions that UWP/WinUI 2 designer availability does not imply the same designer surface exists for WinUI 3 desktop apps.
must_not: Claims installing a missing NuGet package will enable a WinUI 3 visual designer.
Tells the developer to convert back to UWP just to edit the XAML visually.
Invents a hidden Visual Studio command that opens a full WinUI 3 drag-and-drop designer.
acceptable_alternatives: Use temporary prototype XAML in a UWP/WinUI 2 project and manually adapt it back to WinUI 3.
Use Blend or design tools only for assets and visual planning, not as a WinUI 3 XAML designer.
Use third-party XAML preview tooling if the answer clearly states it is not built into Visual Studio for WinUI 3.
solved: The answer tells the developer that the project is not misconfigured, names WinUI 3's lack of a built-in visual XAML designer, and suggests at least one realistic workflow for layout iteration.
partial: The answer says there is no designer but gives little or no practical replacement workflow.
notes: Visual Studio and WinUI tooling change over time; grade against the fixture's WinUI 3 desktop project and the absence of a full visual designer, not against unrelated XAML editors.
